title: `update`/`delete` RBAC on applications no longer covers their managed resources

detection.reason: RBAC policies are the VALUE of argocd-rbac-cm's `policy.csv` key; ConfigMap values are not collected

quote: Starting with v3, the `update` or `delete` actions only apply to the application itself. New policies must be defined to allow the `update/*` or `delete/*` actions on an Application's managed resources.
remediation: Add `applications, update/*` and `applications, delete/*` rows for every role that must keep acting on managed resources, or set `server.rbac.disableApplicationFineGrainedRBACInheritance: "false"` in argocd-cm to keep the v2 behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-rbac-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.policy\.csv}' | grep -E '^p, *[^,]+, *applications, *(update|delete),' # rows printed stop covering managed resources at 3.0 unless a matching update/* or delete/* row exists

title: Logs RBAC is enforced by default — the pod Logs tab disappears without an explicit `logs, get` grant

detection.reason: the affected condition is the ABSENCE of `policy.default` in argocd-rbac-cm combined with the value of `server.rbac.log.enforce.enable` in argocd-cm; only key names are collected and absence of a key is not a projected fact

quote: Starting from 3.0, this flag is removed and the logs RBAC is enforced by default, meaning the `logs` tab on `pod` view will not be visible without granting explicit `logs, get` permissions to the users/groups/roles requiring it.
remediation: Before upgrading, add `p, role:<role>, logs, get, */*, allow` to every role that has `applications, get` (or a default policy that does), unless `server.rbac.log.enforce.enable: "true"` was already set or `policy.default` is `role:readonly`/`role:admin`. Remove the flag from argocd-cm afterwards.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-rbac-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.policy\.default}'; echo; kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.server\.rbac\.log\.enforce\.enable}' # affected when the first line is empty AND the second is empty or false

title: argocd-cm ships default `resource.exclusions` — high-churn kinds stop being tracked

detection.reason: whether any Application syncs one of the newly excluded kinds is not related in the inventory; only the presence of your own `resource.exclusions` key is

quote: Argo CD manifest now contains a default configuration for `resource.exclusions` in the `argocd-cm` to exclude resources that are known to be created by controllers and not usually managed in Git.
remediation: If you manage Endpoints, Leases, CertificateRequests, Kyverno reports or Cilium identities through Argo CD, override or remove the default `resource.exclusions` in argocd-cm; otherwise nothing to do.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.resource\.exclusions}' | head -c 600 # empty = the 3.0 defaults take effect; non-empty = your list wins, check it still covers what you need

title: `argocd_app_sync_status` / `argocd_app_health_status` / `argocd_app_created_time` metrics are removed

detection.reason: the env var that re-enabled these metrics (`ARGOCD_LEGACY_CONTROLLER_METRICS` on the application controller) is not collected — container environment names are not part of the projection

quote: Starting with 1.5.0, these metrics are only available if `ARGOCD_LEGACY_CONTROLLER_METRICS` is explicitly set to `true`. If it is not set to true, you can safely upgrade with no changes.
remediation: Move dashboards and alerts to the labels on `argocd_app_info` before upgrading if the controller runs with `ARGOCD_LEGACY_CONTROLLER_METRICS=true`.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get sts argocd-application-controller -o json 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[].env[]? | select(.name == "ARGOCD_LEGACY_CONTROLLER_METRICS") | .name + "=" + (.value // "(valueFrom)")' # printed = the legacy metrics are on (also check a Deployment-shaped controller)

title: Dex SSO: the RBAC subject switches from the `sub` claim to `federated_claims.user_id`

detection.reason: the Dex connector configuration is the VALUE of argocd-cm's `dex.config` key; ConfigMap values are not collected

quote: If you were using the Dex sub claim in RBAC policies, you will need to update them to maintain the same access.
remediation: Decode the current `sub` claims bound in argocd-rbac-cm (`g, <subject>, role:...`) to their `user_id` and rewrite those bindings before upgrading; users and CLIs must re-login to get tokens with the new claims.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-rbac-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.policy\.csv}' | grep -E '^g, ' | head -40 # bindings printed on a Dex-issued sub claim must be rewritten to the federated user_id

title: Repositories declared in argocd-cm are no longer read

detection.reason: ConfigMap KEY names are collected, never values — this rule fires on the presence of the key in the named ConfigMap

quote: Before repositories were managed as Secrets, they were configured in the argocd-cm ConfigMap. The argocd-cm option has been deprecated for some time and is no longer available in Argo CD 3.0.
remediation: Convert every entry under `repositories`, `repository.credentials` and `helm.repositories` in argocd-cm into a repository Secret (label `argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: repository` / `repo-creds`) before upgrading; Applications on those repositories fail to fetch afterwards.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o json | jq '.data | keys[] | select(. == "repositories" or . == "repository.credentials" or . == "helm.repositories")' # any key printed = repository config that 3.0 ignores

title: ApplicationSet nested selectors are always applied — generated Applications may disappear

detection.reason: composite presence projection: the agent emits nestedSelectorsUnapplied=true only when a selector sits inside a matrix/merge child generator AND applyNestedSelectors is unset or false — an ApplicationSet that already opted in (applyNestedSelectors: true) changes nothing at 3.0 and is not named

quote: Starting in Argo CD 3.0, the field is ignored, and behavior is always the same as if `applyNestedSelectors` was set to `true`. In other words, nested selectors are always applied.
remediation: For each ApplicationSet named here whose `applyNestedSelectors` is unset or false, remove the nested selectors (they were being ignored) before upgrading — otherwise they start filtering and the Applications they exclude get pruned.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applicationsets -A -o json | jq -r 'def nested: .generators[]? | (has("selector") or ((.matrix?, .merge?) | select(. != null) | nested)); .items[] | select(.spec.applyNestedSelectors != true and any(.spec.generators[]? | (.matrix?, .merge?) | select(. != null); nested)) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed have a generator-level selector under a matrix/merge child (not the cluster-secret selector inside clusters), which starts applying at 3.0

title: Bundled Helm 3.17.1: a `null` object in values.yaml now overrides the subchart value

detection.reason: Helm values files live in Git; which Helm-rendered Application carries a `null` object in its values cannot be settled from the cluster

quote: In Helm 3.17.1, this behavior changed and `null` object in `values.yaml` still results in this warning upon performing `helm template`, but the resulting K8s object will be overridden with the invalid `null` value.
remediation: Run `helm template` with Helm 3.17.x over every Helm-rendered Application and remove `null` objects from values files that produce the `cannot overwrite table with non table` warning — they now render as null.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.source.helm != null or ([.spec.sources[]?.helm] | any(. != null))) | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # Applications printed render through Helm — check their values files for null objects

title: Resource tracking switches from labels to annotations by default

detection.reason: the affected condition is `application.resourceTrackingMethod` being ABSENT or `label` in argocd-cm; only key names are collected, and absence is not a projected fact

quote: The default behavior for tracking resources has changed to use annotation-based tracking instead of label-based tracking.
remediation: Either set `application.resourceTrackingMethod: annotation` deliberately before upgrading, or opt out with `label`. After switching, sync every Application once (even if in sync) so orphan detection works on the next sync; resources you track by label outside Argo CD need the tracking annotation instead.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.application\.resourceTrackingMethod}' # empty or label = the default switch to annotation tracking applies at 3.0

title: Applications with `ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true` must be synced explicitly after the tracking switch

detection.reason: presence-only projection of the Application spec, as the agent emits it (keys, never repository URLs or credentials)

quote: If you are using label-based tracking, it is also important to detect whether you have Applications that use `ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true` syncOptions, as such Applications are likely to have orphan resources after switching to `annotation` tracking method and need to be synced explicitly right after the upgrade.
remediation: Right after upgrading, run an explicit sync WITHOUT `ApplyOutOfSyncOnly` on each Application named here (UI, or the API with the option cleared) so their resources receive the tracking annotation; otherwise they read as orphans.
verifyCommand: kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.syncPolicy.syncOptions[]? == "ApplyOutOfSyncOnly=true") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # names printed need an explicit full sync after the upgrade

title: `cluster.inClusterEnabled: "false"` — in-cluster Applications become Unknown and cannot sync

detection.reason: the setting is the VALUE of an argocd-cm key; ConfigMap KEY names are collected, values are not

quote: When `cluster.inClusterEnabled: "false"` is explicitly configured, Applications currently configured to sync on the in-cluster cluster will now be in an Unknown state, without the possibility to sync resources.
remediation: Before upgrading with in-cluster disabled, migrate or clean up every Application whose destination is `https://kubernetes.default.svc` / `in-cluster` (re-enable in-cluster temporarily to delete them cleanly).
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.cluster\.inClusterEnabled}'; echo; kubectl get applications -A -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.destination.server == "https://kubernetes.default.svc" or .spec.destination.name == "in-cluster") | .metadata.namespace + "/" + .metadata.name' # affected when the first line is false and names follow

title: argocd-cm ships default `resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates` — status churn no longer triggers refreshes

detection.reason: whether any Application depends on status-driven refreshes is runtime behaviour; only your own `resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates` keys are collected, by name

quote: Argo CD manifest now contains a default configuration for `resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates` in the `argocd-cm` to exclude common resources that are often mutated in Kubernetes.
remediation: Override or remove the default `resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates` entries in argocd-cm if you rely on refreshes triggered by `.status` changes; otherwise nothing to do.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o json | jq -r '.data | keys[] | select(startswith("resource.customizations.ignoreResourceUpdates"))' # keys printed are your overrides; none = the 3.0 defaults apply

title: Resource health leaves the Application CR's `.status.resources[]` — tools parsing it break

detection.reason: `controller.resource.health.persist` is the VALUE of an argocd-cmd-params-cm key; values are not collected, and which tools parse Application status is not on the cluster

quote: The health status of each object used to be persisted under `/status` in the Application CR by default. Any health churn in the resources deployed by the Application put load on the application controller. Now, the health status is stored externally.
remediation: Point tooling that reads `.status.resources[].health` at the argocd CLI/API instead, or set `controller.resource.health.persist: "true"` in argocd-cmd-params-cm to keep the old behaviour.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cmd-params-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.controller\.resource\.health\.persist}' # empty = health leaves the Application status at 3.0; true = kept

title: Config management plugins now receive empty environment variables

detection.reason: what a plugin sidecar does with an empty environment variable is plugin code, not inventory

quote: In Argo CD 3.0, empty environment variables are now passed to config management plugins.
remediation: Check plugin scripts that test for a variable being unset — an empty string is now passed where the variable used to be absent.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get deploy argocd-repo-server -o json | jq -r '.spec.template.spec.containers[1:][].name' # names printed are plugin sidecars whose scripts may now see empty variables

title: System-level `ignoreDifferences` now also ignore resource updates

detection.reason: whether a field you ignore in diffs must still trigger a refresh is runtime behaviour; only the `resource.customizations.ignoreDifferences` key names are collected

quote: By default, the existing system-level `ignoreDifferences` customizations will be added to ignore resource updates as well.
remediation: Set `ignoreDifferencesOnResourceUpdates: "false"` in argocd-cm if a field you ignore in diffs must still trigger a refresh when it changes.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o json | jq -r '.data | keys[] | select(startswith("resource.customizations.ignoreDifferences"))' # keys printed now also suppress refreshes on those fields

title: `.status` is ignored in diffs for all resources, not only CRDs

detection.reason: whether any desired state intentionally includes a `.status` block lives in Git, not in the inventory

quote: By default, the compare options to ignore the status field has been changed from `crd` to `all` resources.
remediation: If a manifest in Git deliberately carries `.status`, set `resource.compareoptions` with `ignoreResourceStatusField: crd` in argocd-cm to keep the v2 default.
verifyCommand: kubectl -n argocd get cm argocd-cm -o jsonpath='{.data.resource\.compareoptions}' # empty = status differences stop being detected for every kind at 3.0

title: CRDs with `spec.preserveUnknownFields: false` show OutOfSync

detection.reason: the CRD projection carries group, kind and served versions, not `spec.preserveUnknownFields`

quote: This means that CRD deployed with Argo CD containing `spec.preserveUnknownFields: false` will be out of sync. To address this problem, the `preserveUnknownFields` field can be removed from the CRD spec.
remediation: Drop `spec.preserveUnknownFields` from CRDs you deploy through Argo CD (it is deprecated in CRD v1), or add an `ignoreDifferences` entry for it on the Application or globally in argocd-cm.
verifyCommand: kubectl get crd -o json | jq -r '.items[] | select(.spec.preserveUnknownFields == false) | .metadata.name' # CRDs printed go OutOfSync at 3.0 if an Application manages them
